chunks: A group of scholars narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, from Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said: A Tawqi' (holy letter) was sent to Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amari, may Allah sanctify his soul, consoling him for his father, may Allah be pleased with him.

One section of the letter reads: 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return,' submitting to His command and pleased with His decree. Your father lived happily and died praiseworthy; may Allah have mercy on him and join him with His friends and masters, peace be upon them. He remained diligent in their cause, striving in what brings him near to Allah, the Exalted, and to them. May Allah beautify his face and forgive his shortcomings.

Another segment reads: 'May Allah grant you abundant reward and excellent consolation. You have been struck by loss, and we have been struck with you; his separation has made you lonely, and us too. May Allah be pleased with him in his return. It was part of the perfection of his happiness that Allah granted him a son like you, who will succeed him after him, take his place in his affairs, and seek mercy for him. I say, all praise is to Allah, for the souls are pleased with your position and what Allah has placed in you and with you. May Allah help you, strengthen you, support you, and grant you success, and be your Guardian, Protector, Caretaker, and Sufficient One.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam's letter say about the deceased father and his son?
ai.summary: This Tawqi' from the Imam to Shaykh al-Uthman highlights the continuity of religious authority through familial lineage, praising the deceased father's lifelong dedication to the Imam's cause and expressing divine gratitude for his son as a worthy successor. It underscores the Shia concept of 'wilayah' extending to the family of the faithful, where the piety of the father is mirrored in the son's capacity to carry forward the spiritual and administrative legacy. The letter serves as both a personal consolation and a theological affirmation of the Imam's ongoing presence and care during the Minor Occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 323 - A group of our scholars narrated to us from Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn Husain Ibn Musa Ibn Babawayh from Ahmad Ibn Harun Fami, saying, Muhammad Ibn Abdullah Ibn Ja’far Himyari narrated to us from his father Abdullah Ibn Ja’far, saying, A holy letter came out to Shaykh Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Uthman Ibn Saeed Amari, may Allah sanctify his soul, consoling him for his father (a.s).

One section of the letter reads: “We belong to Allah and to Him do we return, we submit to His command and are pleased with His destiny. Your father lived fortuitously and died praiseworthy. May Allah have mercy on him and take him to the company of his Imams and his masters (a.s). He was always dedicated to their cause and diligent in what would take him near Allah, the Exalted, and the Imams. May Allah beautify his visage and forgive him his shortcomings.”

Another segment of the letter reads: “May Allah increase upon you the reward and may He adorn for you the grief. This tragedy has struck you and us. His separation has left you in fright and us too. May Allah please him in his eternal abode. Of the best of his fortuitousness was that Allah gave him a son like you, to stay behind him and take his place and perform his tasks and seek mercy for him. I say, all praise belongs to Allah, for hearts are pure and pleased at your position and at what Allah has bestowed you. May Allah help you, strengthen you, empower you and grant you success. May He be your Guardian, Protector and Guide, and Allah is sufficient for you.”
